text: {"findings":[{"type":"POLICY_REVIEW","title":"Generative AI and photo data used without recorded review","detail":"The proposal generates instructions from past pickup photos, which involves generative AI and potentially personal data (people, license plates, store staff in photos). No legal, privacy, or AI governance review is recorded; only a dependency on the store systems team is listed.","evidence_quote":"Generate store-specific pickup instructions from past pickup photos and show them in the driver app.","citations":[],"recommendation":"Record privacy/legal and generative AI policy review (photo data use, PII redaction, content accuracy checks) before launch."},{"type":"WEAK_EXPERIMENT_DESIGN","title":"Non-random assignment and short duration","detail":"Markets are self-selected by volunteering managers, which introduces selection bias and is not randomization. Duration of 3 weeks is acceptable on the 14-day minimum, but the MDE of 1 point is unclear and inconsistent with the target of a $0.15 cost reduction (about 2%) and the 10-week success timeframe. The pilot also ends well before the 10-week target window.","evidence_quote":"Run a pilot in the markets whose managers volunteer and compare against the remaining markets. Duration: 3 weeks.","citations":[],"recommendation":"Randomize at the store or market level (e.g., matched-market or stratified random assignment), set the MDE in the units of the primary metric consistent with the $0.15 target, and align duration with the metric timeframe."},{"type":"MISSING_GUARDRAIL","title":"Missing guardrails for delivery timeliness and driver experience","detail":"The change affects driver pickup behavior and wait time, but only Delivery Defect Rate is a guardrail. Pickup time/delivery lateness, driver experience or support contact rate, and instruction accuracy are not guarded.","evidence_quote":"Delivery Defect Rate: stop if it rises by more than 0.2 points.","citations":[],"recommendation":"Add guardrails such as on-time delivery rate, pickup wait time, driver support contacts per delivery, and incorrect-instruction reports."},{"type":"UNSUPPORTED_CLAIM","title":"Problem claim lacks quantification and verifiable source","detail":"The problem says associates spend time answering drivers, citing only a generic survey, with no figures. The baseline cost of $7.40 is also given without a source. The sizing of the problem is unverifiable.","evidence_quote":"Store associates spend time answering drivers who cannot find the pickup counter (source: LMD store operations survey).","citations":[],"recommendation":"Quantify the problem (time spent, frequency) with a specific dataset and cite a source for the $7.40 baseline."},{"type":"NO_BASELINE_TARGET","title":"Success metric is weakly linked to the intervention","detail":"Cost Per Delivery has a baseline, target, and timeframe, but there is no metric measuring the actual problem (drivers unable to find the pickup counter, such as pickup search time). Cost per delivery is too noisy and distant to detect the effect.","evidence_quote":"Cost Per Delivery: from $7.40 to $7.25 within 10 weeks.","citations":[],"recommendation":"Add a primary metric tied to the problem, such as pickup duration or associate assist rate, with baseline, target, and timeframe."}]}
